title: Feature flags + rollout tooling for hosted residency enforcement (canary cohorts, kill-switch)
author: Jada Williams
description: Context: Hosted data residency enforcement is rolling out behind flags with canary cohorts and a kill-switch to reduce blast radius as gateway/router/storage enforcement goes live. This PR adds feature flag scaffolding, cohort selection logic, and minimal operator tooling so we can: (1) enable enforcement for a small allowlist, (2) gradually expand by deterministic cohorting, and (3) immediately disable enforcement globally (or per-region) during incidents without code rollback. What’s included: Flags: residency_enforcement.enabled (master gate), residency_enforcement.mode ("observe" | "enforce"), residency_enforcement.canary.enabled (cohorting gate), residency_enforcement.canary.percentage (0-100), residency_enforcement.canary.org_allowlist (explicit allowlist), residency_enforcement.disable_regions (comma-separated list, used as emergency region kill-switch), residency_enforcement.allow_cross_region_fallback_override (guard for explicit override path in routing PR 18452). Cohort selection: deterministic hash(org_id) -> [0, 9999] with percentage rollout, plus explicit allowlist precedence; excludes non-enterprise tiers by default unless explicitly allowlisted (configurable in flag payload). Kill-switch behavior: if master gate off, or region is disabled via disable_regions, the policy evaluator returns residency decision=SKIP (with audit note) and gateway/router treat residency as not applicable; metrics still emit the “skipped_by_flag” tag so we can track exposure. Operator tooling: adds an internal admin endpoint to set/get rollout flags (rbac-protected) and a small CLI script for SRE/Release train to: list cohorts, validate % math, and generate a “canary cohort report” (orgs enabled, region distribution, tier). Observability hooks: adds tracing attrs + counters for cohort_decision (allowlist/percentage/disabled_region/master_off) and exposes a single gauge residency_rollout_enforcement_mode{region} for dashboards. Notes / alignment: This intentionally does NOT change core enforcement semantics (those are in gateway middleware / router / downstream storage checks). This PR is meant to be merged first so subsequent PRs can key off a consistent flag contract. Related: ENG-2842 gateway enforcement PR 18435, ENG-2843 routing constraints PR 18452, audit events PR 18466, metrics PR 18473. Rollout plan: Start in observe mode for 5% allowlisted enterprise orgs in eu-west, then flip enforce for 1-2 orgs, expand to 10%, then 25% gated by violation rates and SLO deltas. If we see elevated denial rates due to misconfig, use disable_regions or master_off and coordinate via runbook-residency-violation-spike.
commits: rollout: add residency enforcement flag contract and defaults
rollout: deterministic cohorting function + allowlist precedence
admin: internal rollout flag read/write endpoints with RBAC checks
ops: add scripts/residency_rollout_cli.py for cohort reporting
obs: add counters/attrs for rollout decision paths
docs: inline README for on-call usage + kill-switch semantics
tests: unit tests for cohorting, precedence, and region disable list parsing
illustrative_snippets: cohorting.ts: const bucket = murmur3_32(orgId) % 10000; const enabled = allowlist.has(orgId) || (canaryEnabled && bucket < percentage*100);
flags.yaml: mode: observe|enforce (default observe), disable_regions: "" (default none), org_allowlist: [] (default empty)
review_conversation: Sean Gallagher: Can we guarantee the kill-switch works even if the flag service is degraded? Right now it looks like we fetch flags from policy-evaluator cache. Suggest: if flag fetch fails, default master_off (fail-safe) for enforcement and emit an explicit metric so we see it.

Jada Williams: Good call. I updated the rollout flag read path so any fetch/parse error returns master_off + mode=observe and increments residency_rollout_flag_fetch_error_total{region}. Also updated the CLI to warn if flags are missing/invalid.
Marcus Lin: Please document precedence in the PR description and in code comments: allowlist > disabled_region > master gate > canary %. Also confirm RBAC: who can write these flags?

Jada Williams: Added a precedence comment above decideResidencyRollout() and updated README. RBAC: rollout_flags:write requires role=release_manager OR sre_oncall; rollout_flags:read available to compliance_admin + sre_oncall. The RBAC bundle change is in this PR (auth/rbac_checks.ts) but the actual role definitions are already in rbac-policy-bundle PR 188.

Naomi Feldman: One product concern: excluding non-enterprise tiers by default is correct, but we should still be able to put a startup pilot into enforce for an early proof. Can allowlist override tier filter?
Jada Williams: Yes — allowlist bypasses tier gating. I also added a flag residency_enforcement.canary.include_non_enterprise (default false) for broader testing when needed.

Amara Diallo: Gateway needs a single boolean to quickly decide whether to run enforcement middleware. Can you export a helper that returns {run_check, mode, reason}? Also please confirm no PII gets logged in cohort reports.

Jada Williams: Added getResidencyEnforcementDecision(ctx) which returns run_check + mode + decision_reason. Cohort report uses org_id (UUID), tier, pinned_region only; no names/domains. Added a note in the tool README and ensured logs are not written by default unless --verbose.

Mina Haddad: Routing override flag name should match router PR 18452 exactly. I see allow_cross_region_fallback_override vs allow_cross_region_fallback. Please align so we don’t ship mismatched flags.
Jada Williams: Renamed to residency_enforcement.allow_cross_region_fallback (and kept a deprecated alias for one release with a warning log). Updated router integration call sites and tests.
Sergio Costa: For dashboards, can we add a gauge that’s easy to query by region: residency_rollout_state{region,mode}? Also add runbook link label on the alert stub?
Jada Williams: Added residency_rollout_state gauge (0=off,1=observe,2=enforce) and included runbook URL in the metric help text + alert annotation stub (will be wired in observability-pack PR 417).

Sean Gallagher: Approving after the fail-safe change and the metric for flag fetch errors. Please make sure on-call docs call out that disable_regions is a blunt instrument and should be used with an incident channel + comms.
Jada Williams: Done. Added guidance + template text in tools/ops/README.md.
release_notes: Internal: Adds feature flags and deterministic canary cohorting for Hosted data residency enforcement, including per-region kill-switch and operator tooling (admin endpoints + CLI) to safely roll out enforcement.
